To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The GENIE application is being successfully wrapped within the Java web service framework.

the use of Web Service technologies has allowed us to: 1) encapsulate the application into components that can be used in different workflows; 2) provide an abstraction that can hide the complexities of the application; 3) allow the application to be composed into workflows in different ways; and 4) provide a mechanism for the application to be deployed and executed in different Grid environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of service-based technologies to the problem of enabling legacy applications for the Grid.
the application of Web services to a legacy application.
the development of a framework that will enable the execution of a complex legacy earth modeling application within the context of a Grid environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has shown that the GENIE application can be made to run within a Web Services-based Grid environment.
this work has been successful in demonstrating how the application has become a more flexible component-based application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application can now be executed within a Grid execution environment, and that this execution can now be managed in a much more flexible and dynamic manner.
we have shown how to take a large, tightly-couple application and enable it for Grid execution by breaking it down into a set of loosely coupled Web Services.
we have successfully shown how the original GENIE application has been wrapped into Web Services and that it is now possible to compose these into workflows for execution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

by wrapping a tightly coupled legacy Fortran application within a component-based environment it is possible to make use of the application within a Grid environment, and that by representing the legacy application as a set high-level components it is possible to compose these into more flexible, higher-level workflows.
by using Web Services to wrap legacy code we can enable the application to be executed within a component based Grid execution framework.

by representing complex legacy applications as high-level, loosely-coupled components it is possible to enable these applications for Grid execution and to make them easier to compose into more complex workflows.
